extracted.intended_audience: prospective DAAD scholarship applicants (international students, graduates, doctoral candidates, postdocs)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of DAAD scholarship programmes, eligibility categories, procedural requirements (calls, deadlines, application portal), selection process, and program-specific rules (e.g., Hilde Domin, In‑Country/In‑Region). Intended to guide applicants on which programmes to consider and what selection criteria apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary target groups / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD scholarships are aimed primarily at graduates, doctoral students and postdocs and are awarded for study and research visits to universities and non-university research institutions in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the baseline eligibility filter when searching programmes in the scholarship database; many DAAD programmes target these career stages specifically. Internships are also funded in some programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research grants for PhD students
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD awards research grants for PhD students from almost all countries of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a PhD student, consult research grant programme calls in the database—these are broadly open to applicants from most countries. Details and exact eligibility are in each call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant for a full doctoral programme — priority for developing/emerging countries
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant for a full Doctoral programme in Germany is offered primarily to applicants from developing and emerging countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from developing/emerging countries should consider full‑doctoral grants; check the specific call for country/region eligibility and required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's degree scholarships — target countries and special programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships for a Master's degree in Germany are available, in particular, for persons from industrial countries. However, some study scholarship programs are aimed specifically at students from developing and emerging countries, such as the 'Study scholarships for STEM disciplines' and 'Development-related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose programmes according to the geographic/country targeting noted in each call (some master’s programmes are for industrial-country applicants, others specifically for developing/emerging countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilde Domin Programme — nomination and eligibility for at‑risk candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Students and doctoral candidates who are at risk of being denied educational or other rights in their country of origin have the chance to get a scholarship from the 'Hilde Domin Programme'. Potential candidates cannot themselves apply for participation in the scholarship programme but are nominated by an institution or organisation that is a legal entity domiciled in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt a direct application; eligible candidates must be nominated by a qualifying German institution. After nomination, DAAD will contact suitable candidates and invite them to apply via the DAAD application portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-Country / In-Region programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: In‑Country or In‑Region programmes offer DAAD funding for a graduate programme, doctoral programme or postdoc period in the applicant’s home country or region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relocation to Germany is not possible, check In‑Country/In‑Region programme calls for funding opportunities in the applicant's country/region; eligibility and benefits depend on the specific programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural requirement: consult call and observe deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to apply for a DAAD scholarship, please read the call for applications for your chosen scholarship programme in the scholarship database, paying particular attention to application deadlines. The scholarship database will take you to the application portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always follow the instructions in the specific call (not the general overview). Missing or incorrect submission relative to the call (e.g., ignoring deadlines or portal instructions) can disqualify an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission path: scholarship database → application portal
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholarship database will take you to the application portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the scholarship database (www.funding-guide.de) to find programme calls and the correct application portal links; do not rely on generic or third‑party submission routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: independent and voluntary selection committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarship applications are reviewed by independent and voluntary selection committees, which also decide on the allocation of scholarships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect peer/expert review by committees; ensure application materials present qualifications and project clearly and professionally for committee assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria used by committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The committees assess the professional qualifications and the quality of the study or research project, but also the potential of the applicant. Special circumstances (e.g. disability) may be taken into account. The detailed selection criteria can be found in the Important Scholarship Information for Scholarship Applicants under point E.3 and in each call for applications under the 'Selection' tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure applications to demonstrate: (1) professional/academic qualifications, (2) a high‑quality, well‑designed study or research project, and (3) applicant potential (future impact/trajectory). If relevant, document special circumstances (e.g., disability). Consult point E.3 and each call’s Selection tab for programme‑specific scoring/weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship benefits and program‑specific allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD scholarships do not have to be paid back. They usually consist of a monthly scholarship payment (currently, for example, € 992 for students and € 1,300 for doctoral/PhD students) and a flat-rate travel allowance. In many cases, DAAD also provides health, accident and personal liability insurance. Depending on the scholarship programme, there are also additional benefits such as a one-off research allowance, family benefits or funds for language courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume uniform benefits across programmes—check the call for the exact benefit package. When budgeting and planning your stay, use the programme’s stated monthly payment, travel allowance and any additional benefits as specified in the call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find detailed selection and programme rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed selection criteria can be found in the Important Scholarship Information for Scholarship Applicants under point E.3 and in each call for applications under the 'Selection' tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For authoritative, program‑specific eligibility, selection, benefit and procedural rules, always consult (a) the Important Scholarship Information (point E.3) and (b) the individual call’s 'Selection' tab in the scholarship database rather than relying solely on the overview page.
